title: The Detection of a Hot Molecular Core in the Extreme Outer Galaxy
question: What are the physical and chemical properties of a star-forming core in a Galactic low-metallicity environment in the extreme outer Galaxy, and how do its molecular abundances compare to inner Galactic and LMC hot cores?

recipe.goal: Extract spectra and measure continuum flux and source sizes
recipe.method: Extract spectra and continuum flux from circular apertures (0.50'' and 1.93'' diameter for SMM1; 0.6'' diameter for SMM2) and fit 2D Gaussians to emission images to measure source sizes
key_parameters: Aperture diameters: 0.50'' (0.026 pc) and 1.93'' (0.1 pc) for SMM1; 0.6'' for SMM2

recipe.goal: Identify spectral lines and measure line parameters
recipe.method: Identify spectral lines using CDMS and JPL databases; fit 1D Gaussian profiles to measure peak brightness temperature, FWHM, LSR velocity, and integrated intensity, or directly integrate over the emission frequency region when Gaussian fits poorly
key_parameters: Assumed line width Delta V = 4 km s^-1 for 2sigma upper limits

recipe.goal: Derive molecular column densities and rotation temperatures
recipe.method: Perform LTE rotation diagram analysis for molecules with multiple transitions, single-temperature LTE calculation for other molecules, and non-LTE RADEX calculations for selected molecules
key_parameters: Exclude transitions with large S*mu^2 at E_u < 300 K for CH3OH, CH3CN, HNCO, SO2, and HCOOCH3
RADEX inputs: n_H2 = 2.1 x 10^7 cm^-3, T_bg = 2.73 K, 10% line intensity uncertainty
assumptions: Optically thin condition and LTE for rotation diagram analysis
Assumed T_rot = 35 K for extended cold molecules, 200 K for compact hot core molecules without rotation diagrams, 36 K for CS/C34S, 39 K for H2CO/HDCO, 166 K for 34SO2

recipe.goal: Estimate H2 column density, visual extinction, gas density, mass, and bolometric luminosity
recipe.method: Calculate N_H2 from optically thin dust continuum emission at 1200 and 870 um and from SED fitting with Robitaille et al. (2007) models; average the two methods to get representative N_H2, n_H2, and gas mass
key_parameters: kappa_1200um = 1.07 cm^2 g^-1, kappa_870um = 1.90 cm^2 g^-1, Z = 0.002, T_d = 60 K (SMM1) and 20 K (SMM2)
assumptions: Optically thin dust emission, uniform spherical gas distribution of diameter 0.026 pc, N_H2/A_V = 2.9 x 10^21 cm^-2 mag^-1

recipe.goal: Calculate fractional abundances and isotope ratios and compare with Galactic and LMC hot cores
recipe.method: Normalize molecular column densities by N_H2 and N(CH3OH) for 0.026 pc and 0.1 pc apertures, apply galactocentric isotope ratios to derive main species abundances from isotopologues, and compute correlation coefficients with Galactic and LMC hot cores
assumptions: 12C/13C = 150 and 32S/34S = 35 at D_GC = 19 kpc; 30% empirical uncertainty on N_H2
